Also note\n55|  `getScheduledQueue` EXCLUDES `failed`, `cancelled`, `waiting_human`, and\n56|  human-stage tasks (L52–70), while the chip number INCLUDES them — so chip\n57|  count and queue length legitimately differ today.\n58|- The exact interaction precedent is `BuildHashTrigger` +\n59|  `ChangelogModal` (`frontend/src/components/layout/`): a right-rail\n60|  element opening a dialog built on the shared accessible `Modal`\n61|  (`frontend/src/components/Modal.jsx`: Escape/backdrop close, focus trap).\n62|  `WidgetManagerModal` is a second `Modal` consumer.\n63|\n64|## Survey synthesis (`SURVEY.md`)\n65|\n66|All five survey questions are still unanswered (`\"answers\": {}`). The plan\n67|therefore carries each question as a decision with a reversible default\n68|(marked [D]), so implementation is unblocked and the operator can still\n69|override before or during implementation:\n70|\n71|| Survey Q | Decision carried by this plan |\n72||---|---|\n73|| q1 — what should the queue number count? | [D] Keep the global open-task meaning for now; make the popup reconcile it (Step 4 + Step 9). Changing the count definition is deferred to Phase 4, conditional on q4. |\n74|| q2 — what should each row show? | [D] Show all five surveyed fields: task name, position, project, current step, waiting/blocked reason. All are already present on `getScheduledQueue` items (`title`, `queueOrder`, `projectName`, `currentStageName`, `priorityReason`/`blockers`). |\n75|| q3 — view-only vs actions? | [D] View-only list + click-a-row-opens-inspector (reuses the existing `setSelectedTask` pattern from the bar). No reorder/cancel — the scheduler owns order and there is no reorder API. |\n76|| q4 — fix the number too, or popup only? | [D] Popup first (this plan's core), number-semantics fix as a separately-gated follow-up step once the popup provides evidence. This is the \"make change easy, then make the change\" split. |\n77|| q5 — which queue number opens the popup? | [D] The bottom-bar chip only — it is the only queue number in the main UI. (Monitor KPI widgets show queue depth too, but only inside the monitor view.) |\n78|\n79|If the operator answers the survey before implementation, the answers\n80|override the [D] defaults. Biggest swing: q4 (\"popup only\" vs \"fix the\n81|number too\") and q3 (full reorder/cancel would need a new backend API and\n82|is currently out of scope).\n83|\n84|## Approach — make change easy, then make the change\n85|\n86|1. **Research spike first (Phase 0).** The one architectural unknown is the\n87|   popup's data source: nothing today serves the GLOBAL ordered queue to\n88|   the frontend (chip = global count, queue endpoints = project-scoped).\n89|   Resolve this before building UI.\n90|2. **Make change easy (Phase 1).** Extract the queue-list rendering and the\n91|   queue-fetch logic into shared units so the popup reuses — not forks —\n92|   the monitor's list. Keep every refactor behaviour-preserving with the\n93|   existing tests green.\n94|3. **Make the change (Phase 2).** Convert the chip to a button opening a\n95|   `Modal` popup; wire the shared list into it.\n96|4. **Then (Phase 4)** decide the count-semantics fix with popup evidence in\n97|   hand — never bundled into the popup diff.\n98|\n99|Big/risky work (data-source decision, shared seams) is deliberately first;\n100|small UI wiring comes after the seams exist.\n101|\n102|## Steps\n103|\n104|### Phase 0 — Research spike: pick the popup's data source (do first)\n105|\n106|- **Step 1.** Confirm what `api.observabilityStatus(undefined)` returns for\n107|  `.observability.queue` when no project filter is set (global or\n108|  active-project?). Read the API route plus one backend test. No code\n109|  changed.\n110|- **Step 2.** Confirm `GET /tasks/queue` without `projectId` returns the\n111|  active project's queue (per `resolveAndGuardProject` in\n112|  `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js`) and check the contract tests in\n113|  `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.test.js` (\"GET /tasks/queue\") for constraints.\n114|- **Step 3.** Decide ONE source (recommendation order):\n115|  - (a) If the observability queue already serves global order, reuse\n116|    `api.observabilityStatus(undefined)` + existing refresh pattern (same as\n117|    `ObservabilityDashboard.jsx`).\n118|  - (b) Else, extend `GET /tasks/queue` with an explicit global mode (e.g.\n119|    `?projectId=all`, mirroring the monitor's `selectedProjectId`\n120|    convention) that calls `getScheduledQueue(store, undefined)`.\n121|    Backend-only addition; no existing contract changes.\n122|  - (c) Fallback: popup shows the active-project queue and labels the\n123|    chip-vs-list scope difference. Only if (a) and (b) are both rejected.\n124|- **Step 4.** Record the decision plus the chip-vs-list inclusion\n125|  difference (`failed`/`waiting_human` counted but not queued) as the\n126|  popup's reconciliation copy (one line, e.g. \"N open tasks counted; M\n127|  shown — failed / waiting-human tasks count but never dispatch\").\n128|\n129|### Phase 1 — Make change easy (shared seams, no behaviour change)\n130|\n131|- **Step 5.** Extract a presentational `QueueOrderList` component from\n132|  `QueueOrderWidget` (props: `items`, `engineState`, `onSelectTask?`,\n133|  `compact?`). `QueueOrderWidget` becomes a thin wrapper. Keep all\n134|  existing `QueueOrderWidget.test.jsx` assertions passing unchanged.\n135|- **Step 6.** Extract a `useScheduledQueue({ projectScope, enabled })` hook\n136|  holding the fetch + refresh + poll logic currently inline in\n137|  `ObservabilityDashboard.jsx`, with `enabled` so it only fetches while the\n138|  popup is open (mirror `ChangelogModal`'s fetch-on-open). Wire the\n139|  dashboard to the hook with no visual change.\n140|- **Step 7.** Add/extend the API client only if Phase 0 picks (b): e.g.\n141|  `api.getTaskQueue('all')` via `flowRequests` in\n142|  `frontend/src/services/flow/index.js`, plus backend route handling and a\n143|  route test.\n144|\n145|### Phase 2 — Make the change (the popup)\n146|\n147|- **Step 8.** Create `QueuePopupModal` in\n148|  `frontend/src/components/layout/` on the shared `Modal`: header with\n149|  count + scope label (e.g. \"Queue — all projects, #1 runs next\"), body =\n150|  `QueueOrderList`, footer = one-line reconciliation note from Step 4.\n151|  States: loading, empty (\"Queue is Clear\" copy consistent with the\n152|  widget), error + Retry (mirror `ChangelogModal`).\n153|- **Step 9.** Convert the bottom-bar chip (`NowPlayingBar.jsx`, L638–666)\n154|  from `div` to `button` opening the modal (precedent:\n155|  `BuildHashTrigger`). Preserve `role=\"status\"` semantics for the count\n156|  (nested live region inside the button, or `aria-label` kept on the\n157|  button), keep the `InfoTooltip`, keep the WCAG 1.4.3 no-text-animation\n158|  contract, and keep the canary overlap gate (`functional.spec.js`\n159|  button-vs-rail rect checks) green. Decide mobile: [D] also render a\n160|  compact chip button on phones OR document that the popup is sm+ only —\n161|  the chip is currently hidden on mobile, so phone users otherwise get no\n162|  entry point.\n163|- **Step 10.** Row click opens the inspector via existing `setSelectedTask`\n164|  (per q3 default); `Escape`/backdrop closes with focus restore (free from\n165|  `Modal`).\n166|\n167|### Phase 3 — Testing plan (runs alongside Phases 1–2, gates done)\n168|\n169|- **Step 11.** Unit/integration (primary gate, `npm run test:unit`):\n170|  - `useScheduledQueue`: fetch-on-enable only, refresh on observability\n171|    event, error state, empty state.\n172|  - `QueueOrderList` / `QueueOrderWidget`: order badges (#1..#n match\n173|    `queueOrder`), active-item single-active invariant, blocked/waiting\n174|    reasons rendered (extend `QueueOrderWidget.test.jsx`).\n175|  - `NowPlayingBar` popup wiring (extend `NowPlayingBar.test.jsx`): chip is\n176|    a button with the queue `aria-label`, click opens modal,\n177|    Escape/backdrop closes, count text unchanged, existing right-rail /\n178|    overlap assertions still pass.\n179|  - If Phase 0 picks (b): backend route test for global mode (order +\n180|    cross-project inclusion), mirroring\n181|    `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.test.js` \"GET /tasks/queue\".\n182|- **Step 12.** Headless UI check (no dev servers): extend or add a\n183|  `npm run capture:screenshot` invocation opening the bar + popup at\n184|  desktop width (and 640px if mobile entry is added) to eyeball layout;\n185|  keep screenshots under the task docs folder.\n186|- **Step 13.** Regression: full `npm run test:frontend` + `npm run test:api`\n187|  (== `test:unit`), plus `npm run lint` for the touched files.\n188|\n189|### Phase 4 — Count-semantics follow-up (gated on q4 answer + popup evidence)\n190|\n191|- **Step 14.** Only after the popup ships: with visual evidence, decide\n192|  whether to redefine the chip (e.g. exclude `failed`, or show\n193|  `queued+active` instead of all-open). Implement as a separate change with\n194|  its own tests (`activeTaskVisibility.test.js`,\n195|  `api/engineStateSnapshot.test.js`) — never bundled into the popup diff,\n196|  so the popup remains a clean before/after debugging lens.\n197|\n198|### Phase 5 — Documentation plan\n199|\n200|- **Step 15.** Update the `NowPlayingBar` / `queueDepth` JSDoc\n201|  (`MARK: queueDepth`) to document click-to-open and the count-vs-list\n202|  reconciliation rule.\n203|- **Step 16.** Add JSDoc `MARK` blocks on `QueuePopupModal` and\n204|  `useScheduledQueue` following the repo's one-function-per-file +\n205|  `@example` conventions (`npm run check:one-function`,\n206|  `check:jsdoc-example` must pass).\n207|- **Step 17.** Short operator note (tooltip / `behindTheScenes` copy + one\n208|  paragraph in the relevant docs page, e.g. the monitor/orchestrator\n209|  guide): what the number counts, what the popup lists, and why they can\n210|  differ.\n211|- **Step 18.** Run `npm run docs:check` if docs pages are touched.\n212|\n213|## Validation Plan (evidence per phase)\n214|\n215|| Phase | Check | Expected evidence |\n216||---|---|---|\n217|| 0 | Read route + observability code, run targeted backend tests | Decision (a)/(b)/(c) recorded; shown by the\n9| *   Now Playing bar's queue popup (and any future queue surface). Data source\n10| *   is the global observability snapshot (`api.observabilityStatus(undefined)`\n11| *   serves every project in dispatch order, so no new endpoint was needed).\n12| *   Fetches on enable only, refreshes on observability invalidations, and\n13| *   keeps a 15 s safety poll plus visibility/focus returns. The monitor\n14| *   dashboard deliberately keeps its own inline fetch: it publishes metrics\n15| *   and queue atomically from one response with monitor-only guards\n16| *   (TASK_UPDATED active-task filter, hidden-tab gating, a staleness rule),\n17| *   which this queue-only hook does not replicate. The return contract is\n18| *   exactly four fields (`items`, `loading`, `error`, `refresh`) — callers\n19| *   destructure those, nothing else. A missing API method surfaces as\n20| *   `error`, never as a silent empty queue; a malformed payload logs a\n21| *   warning and fails safe to an empty list.\n22| * @example const { items, loading, error, refresh } = useScheduledQueue({ projectScope: 'all', enabled: isOpen })\n23| * @param {Object} [opts]\n24| * @param {string} [opts.projectScope='all'] - 'all' or a project id.\n25| * @param {boolean} [opts.enabled=false] - Fetching is off until this is true.\n26| * @returns {{\n27| *   items: Array<Object>,\n28| *   loading: boolean,\n29| *   error: string|null,\n30| *   refresh: () => void,\n31| * }}\n32| ***/\n33|export function useScheduledQueue({ projectScope = 'all', enabled = false } = {}) {\n34|  const [items, setItems] = useState([]);\n35|  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);\n36|  const [error, setError] = useState(null);\n37|\n38|  const mountedRef = useRef(true);\n39|  const fetchInFlightRef = useRef(false);\n40|  const pendingRefreshRequestedRef = useRef(false);\n41|\n42|  useEffect(() => {\n43|    mountedRef.current = true;\n44|    return () => {\n45|      mountedRef.current = false;\n46|    };\n47|  }, []);\n48|\n49|  const fetchQueue = async (refresh = false) => {\n50|    if (!enabled) return;\n51|    if (fetchInFlightRef.current) {\n52|      if (refresh) pendingRefreshRequestedRef.current = true;\n53|      return;\n54|    }\n55|    fetchInFlightRef.current = true;\n56|    pendingRefreshRequestedRef.current = false;\n57|    if (mountedRef.current) {\n58|      setLoading(true);\n59|    }\n60|    try {\n61|      const projectId = projectScope && projectScope !== 'all' ?
